text:
Toronto beat the Islanders 2-1 at Scotiabank Arena, but the first twelve minutes did most of the work. Colton Sissons tipped one in at 7:14 of the first, a 9 percent chance that Nick Paul and Easton Cowan set up. Cowan then scored on the power play at 11:55, a wrist shot that carried a 36 percent chance, and Toronto led 2-0. In that period the Leafs out-chanced New York 1.24 expected goals to 0.44.

After that, the game tilted the other way. New York took 68 shot attempts to Toronto's 48 and held the edge in chance quality in both the second (0.95 to 0.65) and the third (1.27 to 0.80). Expected goals finished almost level, 2.69 for Toronto and 2.67 for the Islanders, but at even strength the Islanders led 1.78 to 1.21. The deserved-to-win number leaned New York, 53 percent to 47. Toronto won on two early goals and one stretch of strong play, not on sustained pressure.

Anthony Stolarz kept it there, stopping 26 of 27 against 2.67 expected goals, good for 1.67 goals saved above expected. Emil Heineman cut the margin with a shorthanded snap shot at 14:09 of the third, assisted by Bo Horvat, who led the Islanders with four shots. Ilya Sorokin stopped 24 of 26 behind a team that blocked only 11 shots to Toronto's 21, but New York never found the equalizer. Toronto also went 1-for-4 on the power play, while the Islanders went 0-for-4.
